text:
tara (CS): Lee from ACME reported a SCIM provisioning issue after their IdP domain merge — users are created but role assignments are inconsistent, and deprovisioning isn't removing roles. Impacting ~12 active users.

lee (ACME SRE): Confirming. Okta SCIM push returns 200s. In product we see users with no roles or with a default \"viewer\" role. Some users are duplicated (old email vs new email). Happening since the domain rename two days ago.

tara (CS): They say the SCIM token is a service account with scopes: `scim.read scim.write openid email`. No extra custom scopes. They did not change the group-to-role mapping in our Console.

ben (eng): Hmm. Two likely failure modes: (1) externalId/username normalization changed during domain merge -> our user-matcher treats as new user -> group->role mapping doesn't apply, or (2) group.externalId values changed on IdP causing mapping lookup to miss. Can you paste a sample SCIM payload and the SCIM audit log line?

lee (ACME SRE): payload snippet:
```\nPATCH /scim/v2/Users/6a9f...\n{\n  \"schemas\": [\"urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp\"],\n  \"Operations\": [{\n    \"op\": \"Replace\",\n    \"path\": \"members\",\n    \"value\": [{\"value\":\"00u1abc\",\"display\":\"alice@acme.com\",\"type\":\"direct\"}]\n  }]\n}\n```
Audit: `SCIM 200 PATCH user 6a9f extId=00u1abc -> created user id u_842`

ben (eng): Thanks. That log line suggests Okta is sending its internal id as `value` (00u1abc) and our provisioning pipeline stored that as externalId. If the IdP then renames or re-issues users during domain merge (new okta id or new email), we can end up with two product users (old extId vs new extId). Our group->role resolution uses group.externalId and user.externalId join; if either changes we won't find existing role bindings.

sam (infra): Quick check: do we still accept `displayName`/email fallback when externalId match fails? Our recent change around immutable externalId stricter matching landed in release v2025.11 — that might be why this surfaced now.

tara (CS): Lee — can you confirm whether the affected accounts show two product users (same email prefix but different extId) or a single user with email updated?

lee (ACME SRE): We see duplicates for 5 users, single mismatch for 7 (no role). Example alice: `u_842` (old extId) and `u_991` (new extId) both exist. Old user still has role, new user none. Deprovision requests delete the old extId user but the role persisted on product side for a bit, then remains attached to a ghost? Hard to tell.

ben (eng): Repro hypothesis: 1) Okta domain merge created new okta internal ids. 2) Okta SCIM did `PATCH members` using new `value` ids -> we created new product users. 3) Our role mapping store keyed by old group->user extId link and we didn't migrate. That would explain missing roles and deprovision oddness.

sam (infra): Immediate mitigations:
- Ask customer to run a one-time reconciliation: SCIM `PUT /Users/:id` for the canonical user to update email/externalId to the original value our mapping expects (or vice versa).
- In Console, temporarily enable email-fallback mapping for that org (we can flip config).

tara (CS): Can you provide the exact curl for the reconciliation so ACME SRE can try?

ben (eng): Example (one-off, run for each duplicate):
```bash\ncurl -X PUT \"https://api.redwood.ai/scim/v2/Users/u_842\" \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc_token>' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{\"userName\":\"alice@acme.com\",\"externalId\":\"00u1abc\",\"emails\":[{\"value\":\"alice@acme.com\",\"primary\":true}]}'\n```
This will align the product user to the IdP externalId we expect. If they prefer we can run a safe migration script on their org (requires approval).

okta-bot: SCIM PUSH 200 OK — requestId=req_7f6b9c — timestamp=1755558990

lee (ACME SRE): We can try the PUT for a single test user. Do you have a recommended order? We want to avoid temporarily removing access.

sam (infra): Test on a non-admin user first. Steps: 1) pick a duplicate pair, run PUT on the product user you want to keep to set externalId -> new canonical id. 2) Confirm roles show up. 3) If good, run for rest in small batches. We will keep audit logging full.

alex (PM): We're capturing this as INC-2025-1443 and assigning to eng-infra + provisioning squad. Priority P1 for customer impact. ETA for triage: 4 hours. Will update ACME and CS with plan.

ben (eng): Longer-term fix options: 
- Add a reconciliation job that detects duplicate emails and merges extId mappings while preserving role bindings.
- Improve fallback matching to prefer email if extId changes within 24h window.
We'll scope after triage.

tara (CS): Action items for CS -> send Lee the one-off curl + warnings and schedule a 1:1 support window while infra runs a read-only discovery first. Sam/Ben please validate there is no race that would flip access during PUT.

sam (infra): Acknowledged. I'll run discovery and post findings in this thread (will include user ids + role states).

tara (CS): Thanks all. Lee, we'll follow up within 2 hours with recommended next steps. :pray:

lee (ACME SRE): Appreciate it — will try test PUT in ~30m and report back.
